\label{lemma-base-change-shriek-flat}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^f \\
Y' \ar[r]^g & Y
}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of $\textit{FTS}_S$ with $g$ flat.
Then there is an isomorphism
$L(g')^* \circ f^! \to (f')^! \circ Lg^*$ on
$D_\QCoh^+(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
stage_b_review_note: At line 4779 the source takes a cartesian FTS_S square with FLAT base morphism g and gives the natural functor isomorphism Lg'^* f^! -> f'^! Lg^* on bounded-below quasi-coherent-derived objects. The draft retains flatness, the correct arrow and bound.
statement:
Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. Suppose
\[
\begin{matrix}X'=X\times_YY'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\ f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y\end{matrix}
\]
is a cartesian diagram in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, where $g$ is flat. Then there exists a canonical natural isomorphism of functors $L(g')^*\circ f^!\xrightarrow{\sim}(f')^!\circ Lg^*$ on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$. It is obtained by applying derived right-adjoint base change to a proper compactification of $f$ and restricting to $X'$. Flatness of $g$ makes the compactification square Tor-independent.
hypotheses: Cartesian square in FTS_S and flat base map g.
conclusions: Upper shriek commutes with flat base change as a natural functor isomorphism.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-shriek-etale}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be an \'etale
morphism of $\textit{FTS}_S$. Then $f^! \cong f^*$ as functors on
$D^+_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
stage_b_review_note: At line 4826 the original asserts f^!≅f^* for étale f in FTS_S on D_QCoh^+. The draft correctly identifies ordinary pullback with derived pullback for étale f and avoids claims about the unrestricted adjoint.
statement: Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. If $f:X\to Y$ is étale, then there is a natural isomorphism $f^!\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*=Lf^*$ on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$. The identification concerns the compactification-based upper-shriek functor, not the generally different unrestricted right adjoint to $Rf_*$ for an arbitrary nonproper étale morphism.
conclusions: The upper shriek of an étale morphism is ordinary pullback.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-locally}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^f \\
Y' \ar[r]^g & Y
}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of $\textit{FTS}_S$.
Let $E \in D^+_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ be an object
such that $Lg^*E$ is in $D^+(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
If $f$ is flat, then $L(g')^*f^!E$ and $(f')^!Lg^*E$
restrict to isomorphic objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_{U'})$
for $U' \subset X'$ affine open mapping into affine opens of $Y$, $Y'$, and $X$.
stage_b_review_note: At line 4876 the source assumes flat vertical f and bounded-below E whose derived pullback remains bounded below; it asserts EXISTENCE of isomorphisms on suitable affine U' mapping to affine opens in X,Y,Y', not global canonical base change. The draft maintains these conditions and only local equivalence.
statement: Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. Consider any cartesian square $X'=X\times_YY'$ with maps $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, and $g':X'\to X$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$. Suppose $f$ is flat and $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ is such that $Lg^*E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_{Y'})$. For each affine open $U'\subseteq X'$ whose images are contained in affine opens of $X,Y,Y'$, the two derived complexes $L(g')^*(f^!E)|_{U'}$ and $(f')^!(Lg^*E)|_{U'}$ are isomorphic in $D(\mathcal O_{U'})$. This is an assertion of existence of local isomorphisms and does not claim they glue to a canonical global base-change transformation.
hypotheses: Cartesian square in FTS_S; f flat; E and Lg^*E bounded below; affine U' maps into affine opens in all relevant schemes.
conclusions: The two upper-shriek base-change objects are locally isomorphic on suitable affine opens, with no global canonical map asserted.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-dualizing-fibres}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
$\textit{FTS}_S$. Assume $f$ is flat. Set
$\omega_{X/Y}^\bullet = f^!\mathcal{O}_Y$ in $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(X)$.
Let $y \in Y$ and $h : X_y \to X$ the projection.
Then $Lh^*\omega_{X/Y}^\bullet$ is a dualizing complex
on $X_y$.
stage_b_review_note: At line 4912 the pinned result assumes a flat finite-type S-morphism and defines ω=f^!O_Y; its derived fibre restriction along h:X_y→X is dualizing on X_y. The prepared statement retains arbitrary y, residue field fibre, derived (not underived) pullback and dualizing conclusion.
statement: Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ and set $\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}=f^!\mathcal O_Y\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$. For any point $y\in Y$ with residue field $\kappa(y)$, set $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ and denote the projection by $h:X_y\to X$. Then $Lh^*(\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet})$ is a dualizing complex on the fibre $X_y$: its restriction to every affine open is the sheafification of a Noetherian ring-theoretic dualizing complex.
hypotheses: f flat finite-type separated over Noetherian S, fibre h:X_y→X.
conclusions: Derived restriction of f^!O_Y to each fibre is dualizing.
